qt: to the Commission Fabio De Masi (NI) Subject:
The EU has withdrawn, on the grounds of the reopening of the Russian pavilion, a grant of EUR 2 million to the Biennale Arte in Venice.1 1.

How is the Commission’s decision compatible with Article 13 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union and Article 167 TFEU, in particular freedom of the arts and the Union’s mandate to respect and promote cultural diversity?

Would the Commission apply the same funding criteria to a national pavilion from Israel, the United States or another third country participating in an EU-funded cultural event in the event that comparable allegations of serious breaches of international law or human rights were levelled against the government in question?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.11.2026) The Commission promotes and protects fundamental rights and is committed to upholding Article 13 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights on artistic freedom and Article 167 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). Culture promotes and safeguards democratic values, fosters open dialogue, diversity and freedom of expression, and should never be used as a platform for propaganda. The decision by the Biennale to allow Russia to re-open its national pavilion is not compatible with the EU collective response to the Kremlin’s war of aggression. As a result of the decision on Russia’s participation in the Biennale of Arts, the granting authority, in this case the European Education and Culture Executive Agency, in consultation with the Commission, terminated the grant agreement. The Commission assessed the Biennale’s compliance with the EU restrictive measures (sanctions) imposed on Russia in the context of its illegal aggression against Ukraine and identified grounds to conclude that breaches of these measures had occurred. These restrictive measures pertain to the Common Foreign and Security Policy of the EU and were adopted by the Council on the basis of Article 29 of the Treaty on European Union and Article 215 of the TFEU. The Commission remains committed to supporting cultural expression and artistic freedom, while ensuring that EU funds are implemented in line with the rules of the EU Financial Regulation1 and other applicable rules.
